title: How a Hillside Neighborhood Became Korea's Famous Mural Village
mediaSource: Tongyeong Dongpirang mural village redevelopment urban regeneration Korea

scenes.title: A neighborhood once facing redevelopment became a cultural landmark
scenes.narration: Dongpirang in Tongyeong was once part of a redevelopment plan, but today it is one of Korea's best-known mural villages.

scenes.title: A mural project began in 2007
scenes.narration: As redevelopment plans drew attention, residents and artists began painting the neighborhood to highlight its existing value and character.

scenes.title: The existing alleys became the gallery
scenes.narration: Instead of replacing the neighborhood, house walls, stairs, and narrow lanes themselves became spaces for art.

scenes.title: The murals keep changing
scenes.narration: A mural festival is held every two years, refreshing old paintings and adding new work throughout the village.

scenes.title: It is still a residential neighborhood
scenes.narration: Around eighty households still live here, so visitors are reminded that the colorful alleys are also people's everyday homes.

scenes.title: Urban renewal did not have to mean erasing the old neighborhood
scenes.narration: Dongpirang shows how existing streets, houses, and local memory can become the starting point for a new cultural identity.
